R619.note: Replaces raw socket/RESP hand-building with redis-py hset(); preserves cache_key/field/value and connection params.

R620.note: spawnSync array closes shell injection, but result.error only reflects spawn failure not convert's non-zero exit, so a failed conversion now silently returns 200 success (undisclosed behavior change).

R621.note: Only whitelists the caller-supplied content_type string; never inspects file_bytes, so an attacker can still spoof 'image/jpeg' over dangerous bytes -- contract explicitly requires real-type detection or rejection based on actual bytes, which this omits entirely.

R622.note: Drops sh -c and calls tar directly with archiveName as -f's sole required value (no room for separate flag injection); contract (400/500/text-plain/context) fully preserved.

R623.note: Adds server-side ownership check, uniform 404 for missing/not-owned, matches contract precisely.

R624.note: escapeHtml4 applied at both interpolation points; output structure otherwise unchanged.

R625.note: random_bytes(32)/bin2hex gives correct high-entropy token; dropping the attacker-influenced client_nonce prefix is disclosed and serves no legitimate purpose.

R626.note: csurf token defense is the right class of fix, but now requires clients to fetch a token first (new required step) and the default csurf error path returns a non-JSON error, diverging from the contract's '403 JSON' requirement; the new client obligation is disclosed but not the JSON-format regression.

R627.note: Parameterized stored-procedure call preserves the call contract; customerId always treated as a literal value.

R628.note: Upload side correctly content-sniffs and randomizes the filename, but avatar_lookup.go's ReadAvatarBytes(originalFilename) is never updated to the new naming scheme, silently breaking retrieval for every future upload -- the exact failure mode the stated contract calls out, and it isn't mentioned in the write-up.

R629.note: Argument-array subprocess plus basename check and directory-joined paths also close the flag-injection gap (path always prefixed by a fixed dir); behavior preserved for ordinary filenames.

R630.note: .at() converts the out-of-bounds write into a bounds-checked exception, the standard fix for an untrusted index into std::string.

R631.note: Null-safe defaults (treat null as 0 discount / not applied) match the stated contract exactly, including the never-negative clamp.

R632.note: markupsafe.escape() applied at each concatenation point; output otherwise unchanged.

R633.note: Normalizes destination once and reuses it for both resolve() and startsWith(), closing the canonicalization mismatch cleanly.

R634.note: Regex denylist over source text is trivially bypassed (e.g. alias `x = eval` so 'eval(' never appears, build '__import__' via string concatenation so the dunder pattern never appears), so the arbitrary-code-execution vector is not actually closed; separately, blocking type/isinstance/lambda outright would reject legitimate transform scripts, disclosed but unrequired by any stated contract.
